mentions.text:
Woah. $ANF exploded +40% today.

You'd think they pivoted from clothes to sell GPUs. But seriously some apparel names are having a big moment recently, especially with $VSXY up 70% YTD.

I don't really focus on consumer apparel in stock research, but I thought it'd be interesting to dive into what's going on because the sector is super uneven and it's kinda interesting. 

Because when you look at peers like American Eagle $AEO, Gap $GAP, Lululemon $LULU, Nike $NKE, Dicks $DKS  ... all getting punished by investors lately.

It's actually pretty simple. The winners are selling stuff people actually want, at full price. 

$ANF grew sales at its existing stores by running LESS promotions, not more. Hollister ran out of inventory because demand was too strong. They've bought back 7% of the company this year and the stock still trades around 11x earnings. So it's a pretty strong story and this brand has completely won over Gen Z.

$VSXY Victoria's Secret is the wilder story. Two years ago this was a dying mall brand. Now same store sales are up 13%, four quarters in a row of growth, and they're taking share in bras from 18 to 24 year olds specifically. 

The new CEO did what she calls a promo detox. They cut the discounts, raised prices, and honestly just leaned into the culture: Hailey Bieber for Valentine's Day, the fashion show back on, and a casting search for new Angels that got 100,000 applicants. Beauty is growing double digits on top of that. Stock went from $21 to $91.

Now look at other brands.

- American Eagle. Last time they reported, inventory was up 27%. Sales at existing AE stores went down. They told the Street margins would shrink because they had to clear product before back to school.

- Lululemon told the Street full price sales in the US went negative and they'd be marking down more this summer to clear inventory. 

- And Dick's just got cut 31% in a day. They bought Foot Locker last year, but the sneaker aisle is on sale and nobody wants to be the one holding the inventory.

- Gap missed on Old Navy seasonal and Athleta was down 12%. 

- Nike is guiding revenue down and telling everyone not to expect things to get better for six months.

What it looks like is that the consumer isn't dead. They're just super picky. If your brand has legitimate heat you get full price and the market pays up. If it doesn't, you discount, your margins go down, and the stock gets smoked.
